knowledge:
- key_parameters: extension=Specifies the extension to handle singleton peptide groups ("2" for 2-peptide rule, "S" for sample-wise correlations, "T" for transcriptomic integration) ;; rna.cond.mask=Vector mapping transcriptomic samples to experimental/biological conditions (used with extension "T") ;; pep.cond.mask=Vector mapping proteomic samples to experimental/biological conditions (used with extension "T") ;; max.pg.size.pirat.t=Maximum peptide group size up to which transcriptomic integration is applied (used with extension "T") ;; titlename=Title for the correlation plot in plot_pep_correlations
- alternatives: The documentation mentions Chen, Prentice, and Wang (2014) parameters, but notes that no automated, heuristic-free methods were previously proposed to find them. No other specific R packages are mentioned as alternatives.
- when_to_use: Use this package when you need to impute missing values (either MNAR or MCAR) in bottom-up LC-MS/MS proteomics data, especially when peptide-to-protein adjacency information is available to leverage peptide groups (PGs).
- pitfalls: Slight imputation variations may occur for peptides belonging to very large PGs because they are randomly split into smaller PGs to reduce computational costs; setting a seed is recommended to ensure reproducibility. Using a small subset of data to fit the prior variance distribution in Sigma (e.g., for the -T extension) is not ideal; it is preferable to use the full dataset for both hyperparameter and Gamma estimation.

workflows.name: standard_imputation_and_diagnostics
workflows.intent: Perform diagnostic correlation analysis and standard imputation on proteomics data.
input: subbouyssie (list containing peptides_ab, a matrix of peptide log-2-abundances, and adj, the adjacency matrix between peptides and proteins)
ropers (proteomics dataset list containing peptides_ab and adj)
workflows.stages: 1. Load the package and dataset ;; 2. Set seed for reproducibility ;; 3. Run standard imputation using my_pipeline_llkimpute ;; 4. Inspect imputed values and parameters ;; 5. Run diagnostic correlation analysis using plot_pep_correlations
workflows.code:
library(Pirat)
library(utils)
data(subbouyssie)
set.seed(12345)
imp.res <- my_pipeline_llkimpute(subbouyssie)
head(imp.res$data.imputed[ ,seq(5)])
imp.res$params
data(ropers)
plot_pep_correlations(ropers, titlename = "Ropers2021")

workflows.name: imputation_with_extensions
workflows.intent: Impute proteomics data using extensions (2-peptide rule, sample-wise correlations, or transcriptomic integration) to handle singleton peptide groups.
input: subropers (list containing peptides_ab, adj, and optionally rnas_ab and adj_rna_pg for transcriptomic integration)
workflows.stages: 1. Load the dataset ;; 2. Run imputation with the 2-peptide rule extension using pipeline_llkimpute ;; 3. Run imputation with sample-wise correlations extension using my_pipeline_llkimpute ;; 4. Run imputation with transcriptomic integration extension using my_pipeline_llkimpute with paired or condition-masked samples
workflows.code:
data(subropers)
imp.res = pipeline_llkimpute(subropers, extension = "2")
mask.sing.pg = colSums(subropers$adj) == 1
mask.sing.pep = rowSums(subropers$adj[, mask.sing.pg]) >= 1
imp.res$data.imputed[, mask.sing.pep]
imp.res = my_pipeline_llkimpute(subropers, extension = "S")
mask.sing.pg = colSums(subropers$adj) == 1
mask.sing.pep = rowSums(subropers$adj[, mask.sing.pg]) >= 1
imp.res$data.imputed[, mask.sing.pep]
imp.res = my_pipeline_llkimpute(subropers,
    extension = "T",
    rna.cond.mask = seq(nrow(subropers$peptides_ab)),
    pep.cond.mask = seq(nrow(subropers$peptides_ab)),
    max.pg.size.pirat.t = 1)
mask.sing.pg = colSums(subropers$adj) == 1
mask.sing.pep = rowSums(subropers$adj[, mask.sing.pg]) >= 1
imp.res$data.imputed[, mask.sing.pep]
imp.res = my_pipeline_llkimpute(subropers,
                             extension = "T",
                             rna.cond.mask = rep(seq(6), each = 3),
                             pep.cond.mask = rep(seq(6), each = 3),
                             max.pg.size.pirat.t = 1)
